title: Closing the AI literacy gap for Main Street can help small business owners do more
summary: AI literacy is key to helping small businesses maximize AI adoption. Learn how education, the AI-WISE Act, and Intuit’s initiatives are helping entrepreneurs grow with AI.

- Closing the AI literacy gap for Main Street can help small business owners do more


Small businesses make up[99.9% of all US businesses](https://advocacy.sba.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/FINAL_FAQsAboutSmallBusiness_2026_012826.pdf) , and for the entrepreneurs behind them, every hour counts. Whether it’s managing day-to-day operations, reaching new customers, or finding opportunities to grow, entrepreneurs are constantly looking for ways to do more with the time and resources they have.


AI is helping make that possible.


According to the[Intuit QuickBooks’ 2026 AI Impact Report](https://www.intuit.com/blog/global-stories/ai-impact-report/) , 77% of US small and midsize businesses now use AI regularly, up from 48% in July 2024. And the benefits go beyond saving time: 78% of businesses using AI report that it has improved productivity, and 43% report that it has increased revenue. Small businesses were also four times as likely to say AI helped increase hiring versus reducing it.


But there’s an important distinction between using AI and knowing how to make the most of it. A lack of knowledge and understanding about AI remains[one of the top three barriers to adoption](https://www.intuit.com/blog/global-stories/ai-impact-report/) , highlighting a gap that could prevent more small businesses from taking full advantage of the technology. Addressing this challenge requires a coordinated effort from the public and private sectors to expand access to AI education, helping level the playing field by equipping small businesses with the knowledge and skills to compete and grow.


## **Greater access to AI education is one of the most direct ways to support small business growth**


Congress can help by prioritizing AI education for small businesses. The Artificial Intelligence Wisdom for Innovative Small Enterprises (AI-WISE) Act offers a step forward. This bipartisan bill, which passed the House of Representatives earlier this year with[Intuit’s support](https://www.congress.gov/119/meeting/house/118686/documents/HMKP-119-SM00-20251118-SD005.pdf) , would require the Small Business Administration (SBA) to build and maintain educational resources on AI tools for small businesses. Legislation like this gives businesses a trusted place to learn what AI can do, evaluate different tools, and build their AI skills responsibly.


The AI-WISE Act ** is one of several proposals in Congress to make AI training more accessible for small businesses. These efforts recognize the opportunity for public and private sectors to work together in bringing AI education to more entrepreneurs and communities.


### **Understanding AI helps small businesses use it with confidence**


The value of AI education becomes clear when small businesses can turn what they’ve learned into action.


For[Lea Landaverde](https://lealandaverde.com/) , a content creator, small business founder, and member of the Intuit Small Business Council, learning how to integrate AI into her business has delivered tangible results: “Learning how to use AI and integrate AI tools into our business has helped reduce our workload by 25% by increasing automation and efficiency with our operations, marketing, and social media.”


Her experience illustrates the real impact AI literacy has for small business owners. Understanding how to use the technology can help entrepreneurs spend less time on routine tasks and more time on what truly matters—running and growing their business.


### **Free, hands-on AI education for small businesses**


To help close the AI literacy gap, Intuit launched the[More with AI Tour](https://publicpolicy.intuit.com/more-with-ai-tour/) in 2025, offering free AI workshops to small and mid-market businesses. The tour began in the US in collaboration with the Initiative for a Competitive Inner City (ICIC) and has expanded to the UK and Canada in partnership with the British Chambers of Commerce and the Canadian Federation of Independent Business.


At each stop, business owners and entrepreneurs discover what AI can do for their business, explore AI tools with hands-on demos, and learn how to use them responsibly. On average, participants[closed nearly 50% of their AI confidence gap](https://reports.icic.org/impact-report-2025/) .


One attendee, Rashida Taylor, CEO and founder of[Stash Candles](https://stashcandleco.com/) , called the Tour a “turning point” in her AI journey. When she attended the Tour, she had only used one AI tool. After attending, she was inspired to use AI more. Now, she uses AI in nearly every part of her business, and credits the Tour workshops with giving her the confidence to do so.


Intuit also recently launched[Activate AI](https://activate.intuit.com/activateAI-Roadshow) , a free, 30-city roadshow designed to help mid-market business and finance leaders understand how AI can support their work and make informed decisions about its adoption.[Kicking off](https://erp.intuit.com/blog/artificial-intelligence/activate-ai-tour-announcement/) at Intuit Dome in partnership with Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, the roadshow features half-day events that bring together expert guidance, real-world examples, and interactive experiences to help businesses adopt AI responsibly and realize its full potential.


## **Intuit believes Main Street + AI does more**


Our goal is to empower small and midsize businesses to use responsible AI with confidence, keeping human expertise and judgment at the forefront of AI. We believe in practical education like the Intuit More with AI Tour and supporting policies that help entrepreneurs access the resources they need.


AI has the potential to transform Main Street, but that opportunity depends on more than technology alone. In the new Congress, passing legislation like the AI-WISE Act can give entrepreneurs the knowledge and confidence they need when it comes to using AI.
